web_evidence.title: The Big Read: The Joy Luck Club Teacher's Guide
web_evidence.note: The National Endowment for the Arts explicitly describes the novel as serial first-person narration moving among multiple participating narrators.

web_evidence.title: Daughter-Text/Mother-Text: Matrilineage in Amy Tan's Joy Luck Club
web_evidence.note: Marina Heung's scholarly structural analysis states that all sixteen chapters are narrated in first person and interweave seven voices.

web_evidence.title: The Joy Luck Club Reading Guide
web_evidence.note: The publisher's author interview confirms sixteen stories arranged in four groups, each preceded by a brief mythlike tale; this explains the local third-person parable passages without establishing an alternating controlling person.

person_note: The sixteen main narratives are controlled by participating first-person voices; having seven narrators does not change the label because all use the same narrative person. Numerous event quotations independently expose sustained I/we narration, and two whole-book Tier B sources confirm the structure. The apparent contrary material in q03064 and q03100 belongs to brief third-person prefatory myths rather than sustained base sections, while other third-person snippets are locally unmarked. Some dialogue buckets appear to contain clipped first-person chapter narration, but this upstream noise does not create a credible person conflict.
